caption_en: 47. Room (J), S wall, section E: on the row of yellow, red and green ashlars, the orthostats are arranged in faux figured alabaster; the yellow floor with the molded stucco frame marks the detachment from the upper area with rows of ashlars.

48. The cubicle (K), recognizable as such by the recesses for the bed in walls E and W, was transformed into a passageway with the opening of the door to the atrium (B), which also involved the cutting of the mighty masonry in opus quadrata of Sarno limestone, visible in the jamb on the right. The decoration was made of large red and yellow panels without figurative motifs that instead appeared in the upper area above with a white background, now completely vanished. The floor was in simple cocciopesto.

49. Tablinum (L): cocciopesto floor with dotted white tiles, dating back to a phase prior to that to which the wall decoration of the fourth style belongs, executed after the room, once open to the peristyle, was walled up on that side. 80 N61474

50. Tablinum (L): even the short stretch of the N wall repeated the pattern of the other walls with a geometric black plinth, a red middle area with a mask vignette and a white upper area with architecture.

51. Tablinum (L), W wall: the black plinth is divided into panels by narrow yellow compartments; the middle area exhibits a large central yellow panel with a vignette (Meleager and Atalanta), separated from the red side panels, also with vignettes (landscapes) but completely illegible. Of the white upper area with architecture, few elements are preserved.

52. Tablinum (L), wall W: shadows remain of the central vignette with Atalanta and Meleager. The young girl is seated on a throne, with her short hunting dress that leaves her legs partly uncovered, she has the long spit resting on her right shoulder and the hat on her lap. Meleager standing, with the spit in his right hand, the dog crouching near him, looks towards Atalanta, while the silhouette of the wild boar abandoned on the ground between the two can no longer be distinguished.
53. Tablinum (L), W wall, S section of the upper white area with architecture.

54. Peristyle (M'): overall view from the S: the entrances can be distinguished from the portico (M) which interrupt the fencing pluteus in which the brick columns are inserted, originally covered with red plaster in the lower part and rough plaster in the remaining part.  80 N61524
55. Peristyle (M°): passage to the W in which there is a cistern mouth with a lava manhole cover.
56. Peristyle (M°): wall E with a black background with plants and birds.   80 N61525

57. Peristyle (M°), wall E in its current state, with the almost total disappearance of pluteus S well preserved at the time of excavation (see fig. 59). In the first panel on the left you could recognize a marshy environment with a heron that had grabbed a snake.
58. Peristyle (M°), wall E, section N: only part of the marsh fauna scene remains facing left.  80 N61526

59. Peristyle (M°), SE corner, when the excavation was completed, with the six underground dolii, some of which were restored in antiquity. The plinth with a black background shows in the panels, birds among bushes, herons among marsh plants, peacocks on branches with fruits facing each other in the two central panels of the S wall. In the compartments, flowering bushes can be distinguished in correspondence with the semi-columns. The remaining part of the wall was covered with rough plaster.
60. Peristyle (M°), S wall with semi-columns, in its current state.
61. Peristyle (M'), SE corner: only traces of the painted plants remain in the compartment and in the panel.  80 N61510
62. Peristyle (M'), S wall: in the second intercolumnium you can recognize the silhouette of the peacock advancing to the right.  80 N61512
63. Peristyle (M°), S wall: in the following intercolumnium the branch with fruit is preserved towards which another peacock advanced facing the previous one, and now no longer recognizable.
64. Peristyle (M'), W wall with semi-columns and the square window of (X). The semi-columns are preserved here up to the modest Tuscan capital.  80 N61509
65. Peristyle (M°), W wall, S section: on the black plinth, among marsh plants, the fight between a heron and a snake took place.
66-67. Peristyle (M°), W wall: in the second intercolumnium there was a quieter representation of a garden with birds among bushes.  80 N61518 - 80 N61519
66-67. Peristyle (M°), W wall: in the second intercolumnium there was a quieter representation of a garden with birds among bushes.  80 N61518 - 80 N61519

68-69. Peristyle (M'), W wall: in the last intercolumnium towards the N the representation of a marshy landscape with a heron in the water € returns, a little further on, another with open wings fighting with a snake, while from above, over the plants, another bird flies to the left.   80 N61521 - 80 N61517

68-69. Peristyle (M'), W wall: in the last intercolumnium towards the N the representation of a marshy landscape with a heron in the water € returns, a little further on, another with open wings fighting with a snake, while from above, over the plants, another bird flies to the left.   80 N61521 - 80 N61517
70. Oecus (N): the floor of this room dates back to the first style in beaten blue, white, black, green and red polychrome limestone.  80 N56764

71. Oecus (N), N wall: the green plinth is completely discoloured on this wall in which the varied polychromy of the first style decoration is preserved with yellow, red and green orthostats separated by ashlars imitating agate and alabaster. A yellow top with stucco kyma reversa separates the upper area consisting of two rows of yellow, red, purple and faux marble ashlars, crowned by a molded stucco frame.

72. Oecus (N), an elongated ashlar with faux marble (agate), which continues on the adjacent wall according to a typically Roman taste, and very common in Pompeii, which prefers the rendering of a continuous scheme that encloses the space without abrupt passages from one wall to another to the original structural meaning of the representation of "real" blocks.
73. Oecus(N), N wall, section E: detail of the faux alabaster plateau subjected to the green orthostate of the middle area. 80 N56762

74. Oecus (N), wall E: on the green plinth the same decoration as on the N wall is preserved, with alternating orthostats and ashlars in imitation marble; of the upper area only part of a yellow and a red ashlar remains.
75. Oecus (N): the W wall also retains conspicuous remains of the first style decoration.

1. Vestibule (A): the walls of this room (here the $ one is visible) were covered with a high black plinth with a red band separating it from the upper white area. On the red band of the S wall the graffiti MVSON was read and on the white plaster COPONII (CIL IV 7100, 7101).

2. Of the atrium (C) the floor and the impluvium are no longer visible, both in cocciopesto with sparse marble flakes. On the eastern side of the impluvium is the cartibulum with a square base and a single podium of fluted travertine and a circular marble top (diameter 88.5 cm). The cubicle (G) with circular window and the tablinum (F) are visible.  80 N61467

3. The atrium (C), like the vestibule, was painted with a high black plinth bordered by a red band, still visible in the S-E corner. The S jamb of the room (1) also preserves remains of the previous decoration of white plaster speckled to adhere to the subsequent pictorial coating.   80 N61455

4. The function of the cubicle of the room (D) is attested by the recess for the bed on the wall S; remains of the decoration with a high black plinth divided into panels by thin red squares were preserved in the N-W corner.

5. Tablinum (F): the arrangement of the decoration in white tesserae in the cocciopesto floor would confirm its use as a triclinium. The threshold with a network of squares placed at each corner is followed by three long rectangular carpets divided by diagonals and the central one also by a lozenge. In the innermost triangle of the side mats is a deer behind it. In the center of the room there is a square carpet containing a circumference within which is a pair of rectangles arranged in a cross and crossed by transverse lines, inscribed in a square placed at each corner.
6. Tablino (F): detail of the threshold of the cocciopesto floor with a net of squares placed at each corner outlined in white tiles and with a black tile at the meeting points.
7. Tablinum (F): detail of the floor carpet on the right with a deer behind it outlined in white tesserae and oriented so as to be observed from inside the room.

8. Tablinum (F): detail of the central carpet bordered by two rows of white tesserae and consisting of a circle within which is inscribed a square placed at each corner containing two crossed rectangles cut by transverse lines.

9. Tablinum (F), wall N: the decoration of phase IIB of the III style, extremely simple, on the other hand, presents a considerable variation in colours. The purple plinth is followed by the plinth divided into panels of which the central one is red and the lateral ones black; the middle area exhibits a verdigris panel in the center, inserted in an aedicule hinted only by the side columns, on the sides yellow panels separated from the red panels of the ends by thin black bands; the frieze was illegible already at the time of excavation; the upper area is white with purple architecture.

10. Tablinum (F), N wall: in the painting of the central panel there is a bullfighting scene that does not seem to refer to a mythological episode, but rather, given the presence of the circular building in the background, similar to an amphitheater, to a real combat of the type included among gladiatorial shows. A galloping bull to the left has been joined by a man in a short red tunic and cloak and high green shoes, who is about to hit him with a spit that he squeezes in his raised right hand. In making this gesture he climbs over another bull lying on the ground killed by the other character in a gray tunic, who holds a spit in his right hand and a red mantle raised above his head in his left. In the background a statue of Priapus stands out on the rocks.

11-12. Tablinum (F): wall E has substantially the same scheme as wall N, but is divided, in the middle area, into three panels, of which the central one is verdigris and the side ones are red. The traces of the slender architecture present in the upper white area are better distinguishable.

11-12. Tablinum (F): wall E has substantially the same scheme as wall N, but is divided, in the middle area, into three panels, of which the central one is verdigris and the side ones are red. The traces of the slender architecture present in the upper white area are better distinguishable.
14. Tablinum (F): the N section of the W wall, interrupted by the large door, has a black background with simple yellow squares. 80 N56755

13. Tablinum (F), wall E: in the central panel with a verdigris background there was a painting (45x40 cm) now completely vanished, in which Schefold proposes to recognize the scene of Marsyas and the nymphs, one of whom plays the double flute, in a landscape with trees and with the statue of Priapus at the top of a kind of pyramid.

16. Tablinum (F): detail of the graffiti inscriptions (CIL IV 6849) whose reading confirms the use of this room as a triclinium. It reads, on six lines: CIIR/XXXI/D.IIIIIIII/SAS XVII / PER. XIIII / COCTI. DVO (CIL IV 6849).
15. Tablinum (F): on the S side of the northern jamb you can clearly read some circles engraved with the compass and higher up engraved inscriptions. 80 N56758

18. Cubicle (H), N wall: section O is the one in which the frieze with schematic four-petal flowers and circular elements above the red panel is best preserved. The conch of the circular window is visible, then walled up in ancient times.

17. The small room (G) is interesting not so much for the simple cocciopesto cladding on all the walls except for the S wall where the same decoration of the atrium was repeated, but for the presence of elements that can partially understand its utilitarian functions. It took light from the arched window, open towards the atrium in the O wall, which also preserves the row of holes for the beams of a roof; on the N wall there remain, at the bottom, the holes for the supports of a shelf, and a masonry balcony, while on the E wall there remains a clay pipe for the conveyance of rainwater.
20. Cubicle (H), wall E: you can barely guess the partition of the middle area into panels, and the presence of bands of different colors in the upper one.
19. Cubicle (H), N wall, section E: on a faded black plinth divided into panels, the middle area is divided into a central yellow panel and a red side panel, both devoid of decorative elements.

21. Room (I), wall E: plants were depicted in the white plinth; the middle area, with a symmetrical structure with a central aedicule supported by slender columns, shows the scene of the Rape of Europa in the center and in the side panels agonistic vases with palm branches. 80 N61452

22. Environment (I): the Rape of Europa, is represented in the moment when the bull carries the girl covered only around the legs by the yellow mantle that she holds with her right hand behind and on her head, in the gesture proper to the aurae velificantes. Figures executed in rapid strokes wander on the bank among the trees.
23. Room (I): in the wall $ the plinth with flowering plants is clearly recognisable, while the middle area was already incomplete at the time of the excavation.

25. Environment(I): detail of the seascape with three ships (disappeared) pushed by the rowers to the right towards the shore on which male figures roam. Sogliano's observation that "the representation is damaged above", suggests that this scene could be the detail of one of larger dimensions, and of a different subject.
24. Room (I): the O wall, interrupted by the door, showed in the S section a competitive vase and in the N section a seascape partially preserved below the protective roof.

1. View of the external façade with the main entrance at no. 29, in which the presence of wooden jambs can be recognized by the imprints in the plaster and, in the center of the photo, the secondary entrance 30 of smaller dimensions.

2. Vestibule (A): on the N wall traces of the IV style decoration were still visible in a square imitation work with blocks outlined in red and black, above the black plinth. On this and on the opposite southern wall some graffiti were read, two of which with the name C. VETTIUS FIRMUS (CIL IV, 6851-6852, 7103-7104).

3. Atrium (B): the E wall (collapsed during the earthquake of 23.11.1980) had, above the door, two small argon niches probably intended to accommodate the imagines maiorum. Above the black plinth ran a sort of predella bordered by red bands, with birds pecking among plants and fruits; the middle area, on the other hand, imitated, as in the vestibule, the square work. The atrium was lit through the large window open onto the courtyard (I), beyond which the entrance to the kitchen (J) can be seen. 80 N61436

4. Room (E): the S wall, like the opposite N wall, was divided into three panels, the central one being yellow and the lateral ones red, with vignettes of birds pecking among plants in the centre, separated by narrow compartments with a white background crossed by garlands. Already at the time of the excavation, faint traces of the red borders remained of the frieze. The red plinth displayed bushes and flowering plants in the panels and compartments.

5. Room(s): the O wall, which had the same scheme as the short ones, with the duplication of the central yellow panel, was interrupted by the two splayed windows, of different shapes, open onto the Vicolo dei Vettii.

6. Room (G): wall E, like the others in this room, has a rough plaster covering contrasting with the value of the marble table, supported by a herm of Silenus in black and antique yellow marble, found inside the room. Interesting is the presence of a fragment of molded tuff frame, partly chiselled to reuse it as a building material, and a closed arched niche, which came back to light with the fall of the plaster.
7. Room (G): detail of the moulded tuff cornice, still partly covered by the rough plaster covering the wall E.
8. Room (G): wall E with the high plinth of cocciopesto and the rough plaster of the upper part. 80 N61440

9. Room (H), N wall: very little remains of the modest red plinth divided into panels with plants. The middle area with a pink background has a bipartite structure with a central compartment between the panels decorated with squares with dolphins facing each other on the sides of vases (?).
10. Room (H), N wall: detail of the picture of section O with dolphins faced, now completely unrecognizable.
11. Room (H), wall E: detail of the red plinth with plants in the compartments and carpet edges in the panels. 80 N61448

12. Room (H): wall S with the door through which you can see the courtyard (I) and, beyond the garden (L), the wall N of the small room (M). The plinth of the E section retained almost entirely a red panel with a single line carpet border.

13. Room (H), S wall: on the O jamb of the door remained, until before the earthquake of 1980, scanty strips of the pink plaster of the middle area with a circle graffiti within which a star traced with a compass was inscribed.
14. Room (H): through the door in the wall O you can see, beyond the atrium (B), the room (E).

15. Cubicle (N), wall E, section S with the recess for the bed that retained scarce traces of the white plaster. With the collapse of the upper part of this wall, any trace of the splayed window in it has been lost.

16. Room (0): the mouth of a terracotta cistern was found in the opposite N-E corner. The walls still retain traces of the decoration with a high plinth of cocciopesto and an upper area of rough plaster. The metal structure in the foreground, at the time equipped with glass, was placed to protect the two blocks of slaked lime found at that point.
17. Environment (0O): two blocks of slaked lime with the imprints of the mats in which they were contained.

18. Room (O): on the plinth was painted an agathodemon serpent crawling from the right, towards the altar placed towards the center of the wall. Documented only by the description of the discoverers, no trace of this lararium remains. 80 N61432

1. The courtyard (G) seen from E: one of the amphorae found in the same room rests on the masonry column covered with red plaster in the lower part and white in the upper part. Behind the terracotta puteal you can see the W wall of the large triclinium (J) with a landscape painting in the central aedicule.

2. Courtyard(G)seen by O in its present state, without the supporting column of the portico, the puteal and the amphorae. On the E wall you can recognize "the window on the left with leftovers of the tiled canopy ... and a small circular opening on the right".

3. Room (H): the decoration of the first style with ashlars in relief was tapped to make the plaster of a later one adhere better. The decoration of the cocciopesto floor with sparse marble flakes also dates back to the primitive construction phase.

4. Triclinium (J), wall O: geometric black plinth. In the middle area you can still recognize the central aedicule with the white background of the landscape painting with cattle and sheep grazing near a watercourse; in the red side panels there were vignettes. Nothing remains of the upper white area with slender architecture.
5. Triclinium (J), wall O: detail of the black geometric plinth with simple yellow lines crossing the panel. 80 N61428
1. Vestibule (A): lava threshold with recesses for the wooden jambs and for the door latch.

2. Atrium (B): the walls were covered with a high plinth of cocciopesto, only the lararium niches placed above the door towards the courtyard (F) were covered with white plaster extended around them to form a rectangle. In the NE corner, on the lower left of the photo, there was the masonry balcony for a wooden staircase to the upper floor.

3. Thermopolium (C): view from the E with the L-shaped counter with a ladder painted in red, for the display of the goods. The virile figure with an erect phallus painted on the N forehead of the same has completely disappeared. The marble mortar was found in the atrium, with which this room is interconnected, together with other bronze, glass and terracotta vessels and fragments of wine amphorae with inscriptions on the neck.

4. Thermopolium (C): the floor is made of cocciopesto with dotted white tiles, interrupted by the recess of lava for the repagulum, the wooden pole that ensured the closure of the door. Note the negative imprint of the threshold which was probably made of wood.

5. Thermopolium (C): front W of the counter with a red background with semi-aedicules with acroterial seahorses, from which garlands are suspended connected to the volutes with vegetable candelabra, surmounting a yellow square within which is an ejaculating phallus. On either side two virile figures in long tunics, advancing towards the center, masturbating.
6. Thermopolium (C): detail of the left section of the front O of the counter in its current state: almost only the contour line remains of the male figure.

7. Thermopolium (C): detail of the right section of the O front of the counter: the figure on the right, which at the time of the excavation was the best preserved, so that it could be described as bald, is even more evanescent than the other.
8. Thermopolium (C), N wall: on a low plinth of cocciopesto, the middle area is divided into schematic panels separated by yellow squares, each with the vignette of a pecking bird.
10. Thermopolium (C), wall N: upper right corner of panel O with STORUS graffiti (CIL IV, 1023b), in which the O seems to have been derived from the correction of a Q.
9. Thermopolium (C), N wall, section O: detail of the vignette with a parrot facing right, with a cherry in its beak, on a flat between seedlings.
12. Thermopolium (C), N wall, section E: detail of the vignette: a peacock on the left, pecking at a plant with flowers (?), on the usual plain.
11. Thermopolium (C): in the central panel of the N wall there is another vignette with a bird on the right with two cherries in its beak, on a flat with seedlings with lanceolate leaves.
14. Thermopolium (C), wall E, detail of the vignette: the cockerel on the left, copiously bleeding, is about to fall, while the other holds the palm of victory in his beak. 80 N61384
13. Thermopolium (C), wall E: the decorative scheme is the same as on wall O but only a short section is preserved near the door towards the atrium, with the vignette with cockfighting.
15. Thermopolium (C), S wall: only in section E are preserved the remains of the decoration on a white background, divided into panels by simple yellow squares.
16. Thermopolium (C), S wall: detail of the vignette with a bird with a long tail pecking its back.

17. Triclinium (E): the E wall, more than the others (the N was already devoid of plaster at the time of discovery) retains details that make the decorative scheme of the III style recognizable. On the black geometric plinth, now completely illegible, the middle area has an aedicule in the center with a landscape painting on a white background and red side panels with vignettes (vases). No elements of the frieze and the upper area are preserved.

18. Triclinium (E), wall E, detail of the painting with a sacred landscape: on a bridge in the center of the composition stands a red column, adorned with thyrsis tied with bandages and supporting a crater; near it are a statuette of Priapus and a club, not far away, on the right a metal crater on which two rods rest. From the right they advance

19. Triclinium (E), S wall, section E of the door towards the atrium: the red panels, separated by the narrow white compartment with a thin candelabrum, had in the center vignettes with a pecking bird on the left and a vase on the one adjacent to the window.
20. Triclinium (E), S wall, W section of the door towards the atrium: in the red panel of the middle area the vignette with a bird on the left on a flat can still be distinguished.

21. Triclinium (E), wall O: the description of the subject of the central painting of this wall, contained in the report of the News of the Excavations, is the only preserved testimony, in the absence of any reproduction. It was recognized although "the representation" had "much vanished" Polyphemus seated on a cliff with a sheep next to him and Galatea arriving from the left, on the back of a dolphin.

22. Cubicle (H), N wall, section O: the black plinth is completely discolored; in the middle area the red panel can still be recognized, crossed by a thin candelabrum expanded in the center in a bulb, from which two filaments hang, placed on the side of the central aedicule on a white background.

23. Cubicle (H), N wall, section E with window and built-in bed. In the white background of the central aedicule you can recognize the frame of a painting (30 x 40 cm) already vanished at the time of the excavation. The red side panel, interrupted by the window, is crossed by the thin metal candelabra with hanging filaments.

24. Cubicle (H), N wall: detail of the upper area section O, on a white background with light aedicules and hanging garlands. No trace remains of the frieze with squares with fruit and pecking birds placed above the middle area.

25. Cubicle (H): on half of the wall E the painted plaster is preserved for the entire height, which allows the proportions between the various parts of its structure to be recognized. On the completely faded black plinth, there is the middle area with a central aedicule on a white background with a picture (30 x 30 cm) between red side panels and a checkered frieze; the upper area was white with light architecture.
26. Cubicle (H), wall S, section E: in the red panel of the middle area the thin metal candelabra that crosses it can be clearly distinguished.
27. Cubicle (H), S wall, section O: only a small part of the central aedicule with a white background remains, while above the red side panel, the checkered frieze can be recognized.
28. Cubicle (H), S wall: detail of the checkered frieze, with birds and fruit now completely illegible, and of the white upper area.

29. Cubicle (H), wall O: there is no description of any figurative details seen at the time of the excavation and now completely vanished, despite the fact that the different areas of the decoration can be distinguished. 80 N61420

1. Bottega (]): threshold made up of blocks of lava and travertine in the central section, with recesses for the portcullis. On the left you can recognize the space for the revolving hinged entrance door.  80 N61413
2. Bottega (]): N wall with a high pink plinth divided into panels by narrow compartments bordered by red bands and crossed by a long shoot. The upper area is made of cocciopesto.

3. Workshop (]): resumption of the S-E angle carried out when the pictorial decoration was still fairly preserved. In the middle area you can recognize the crowning of the panels with horizontal bands ending at the ends with squares containing a four-petal rosette.

4. Bottega (}): corner S-E in its current state. At the bottom right, you can recognize the balcony for the staircase leaning against the E wall and the vertical clay pipe inserted in the latter for the disposal of water on the upper floor. 80 N61406

1. Cubicle (D): the N wall, reinforced by the insertion of the brick terminal, was covered with white plaster with a low plinth with small squares outlined in red and a middle area divided into panels by equally simple red frames.

2. Cubicle (D): in the N-E corner there are remains of the fourth style decoration on a white background, the gaps of which allow us to see the restorations of tuff and bricks in the N section of the door. Above the latter is preserved the plaster of a previous decoration, tapped to adhere to that of the last period of the life of the house. In the background is the iron and glass structure that protected the impluvium already severely degraded in 1980.
3. Cubicle (E): a high plinth of cocciopesto covered the walls of this room which "took light from the small window on the S wall.

4. In the S-E corner of the corridor (G) there is a dolio used as the mouth of the cistern into which the rainwater collected through the shaft (F) located beyond the plastered wall visible on the right flowed.   80 N61371

5. Triclinium (H): in the N-W corner of this room a pile of lime was found, near the door of the apotheca obtained in the basement. The walls were covered with a high plinth of cocciopesto, which left room in the upper area for simple rough plaster.

1. Viewed, up to the other clinio (i) in the background, by the rooms (C) and (D) separated by brick pillars of which only the N remains covered, like the rest of the walls, by a high plinth of cocciopesto on which the upper area developed in simple white plaster. The southern wall has been reconstructed in its entirety on the 5 pile of structures identified at the time of the excavation. 80 N61356

2. The peristyle (G), seen from the W, had porticoes on the N, E and W sides. 'Between the columns, covered with white plaster there were plutei with planters, interrupted in the southern sections of both sides, to allow access to the garden and to accommodate, on the W side, the mouth of an earthenware cistern. 80 N61355

3. peristyle (G), S wall with aedicule lararium with pediment supported by two columns with abacus. The exterior was covered with white plaster, inside the niche, painted with birds, runs a low plinth leaning against the walls, on which two oil lamps were found. The table placed in its original position has a rectangular marble top and a monopodium, whose molded base is not visible, in travertine.

5. Peristyle (G): on the back wall of the lararium aedicule, a long-tailed bird, facing left, holds three cherries in its beak. The disappearance of the color of the head does not allow the breed to be recognized. A festoon consisting of three garlands connected by thin tapeworms and red fruits closes the square bordered in red at the top.
4. Peristyle (G): inside the E wall of the lararium aedicule there is a painted bird, whose tail can be distinguished, facing the back wall.   80 N61360

6. Peristyle (G): the O wall of the lararium aedicule also has a bird, a pigeon, facing the back wall. At the top, a festoon of garlands and fruits completes the decoration, framed within red borders.  80 N61361

7. Peristyle (G): the aedicule had a small vault decorated with colorful dotting, turned in the N-S direction. In the lunettes, of which the O one is preserved, branches with pomegranates were painted.
8. Triclinium (H): overall view from the west of the current state, with the walls and roof restored.   80 N59554

9a-b. Triclinium (H): the threshold in black and white mosaic, to which a marble slab was superimposed on the Ne and a travertine slab on the S, for the wooden jambs and the hinges of the door, dates back to the III style and showed two branches of acanthus rising from a central tuft. The border consists of two black bands.

9a-b. Triclinium (H): the threshold in black and white mosaic, to which a marble slab was superimposed on the Ne and a travertine slab on the S, for the wooden jambs and the hinges of the door, dates back to the III style and showed two branches of acanthus rising from a central tuft. 179a-d. During the excavation of the garden in front of the triclinium (31), carried out in 1985, numerous and minute fragments of painted plaster were recovered in the filling soil, pertaining to an articulated and refined wall of phase IIB of the III style. The elements available allow the reconstruction of a large room, with decoration with a symmetrical structure, probably divided into an antechamber and hall; one can therefore think of a triclinium redecorated following heavy damage, or rebuilt following substantial structural changes. A panel with a black background was almost entirely recomposed flanked by an architectural foreshortening with a blue background beyond which another panel with a black background returned. The fragmentary nature of the plaster does not prevent us from appreciating the richness of the decorative motifs, animated and otherwise, and the high technical quality of the very accurate drawing even in details far removed from the viewer's eye, such as those of the frames and squares in the upper area. The black plinth with taut garlands and small squares is distinguished from the predella by a band with upside-down lotus buds and semicircles. The predella follows the course of the architecture of the middle area, curving in correspondence with the pinkish marble base with reliefs of sphinxes facing corresponding to the colonnaded hemicycle of the foreshortening. Groups of Maenads, Silenus and Satyr (fig. 179d), in different attitudes and activities, each of which is concluded in itself, constitute a unitary subject, which can also be read below. A stretched Maenad playing the lyra facing a Silenus playing the double flute seem to accompany the coronation of the seated Maenad, performed by another standing; extremely lively is the dance of the following Maenad who, seen from behind with her mantle raised, holds a tray in her left hand, towards which she looks; followed by the group consisting of the Maenad cloaked in green looking towards the Satyr running with a Maenad on his back; of a fourth figure only a hand remains, while on the far right there is still a seated Maenad, dressed in green, looking downwards. The black panel of the middle area (fig. 1'79a) is framed by taut garlands, rising from a crater flanked by panthers, consisting of daisies and bunches of grapes to which pomegranates are added after the interruption, at a third of the height, marked by the presence of a pair of winged griffins standing on a goblet base; higher up another interruption is given by a Mermaid in frontal view, while the terminal element is represented by an eagle placed in front of the capital of the column that guarantees the first element of the side foreshortening. In the latter (fig. 1'79b) Ionic columns, beyond which windowed walls can be seen, stand out to support a curved architrave, decorated with masks alternating with panthers, on which rest two theatrical masks and a female figure with cornucopia and modio on her head, placed in correspondence with the column with collars and lotus buds, which closes the foreshortening on the left and which at the base presents the mask of a young Satyr. Particular for its exuberant decorative richness is the red partition (fig. 179c) that closes it at the bottom; on its surface there are vine branches, pine branches with a pine cone, wild roses, ivy with corymbs, pears, oleanders, on which stand out the masks of a young Satyr and an elderly Silenus, a silver situla, a five-reed syringe, a cist and a goat's head. The dividing element towards the next black panel consists of a reed around which an oak branch with acorns and one of white bellflower in bloom are wrapped on which a snail and a lizard move. The upper area has a yellow background with garlands and shoots that delimit an ovular element with a black background with a Maenad prone towards a kneeling Satyr, in correspondence with the black panel, while in correspondence with the foreshortening, on a red background, there is a painting with the busts of a Satyr crowned with pine and a Maenad crowned with ivy. Also in this area the shoots are enriched with fruits, accompanied by floral cusps and paintings with animals.

Gym (C); the shot from the S-W corner of the room allows us to recognize on the left the stretch of wall in opus incerta above the S colonnade, decorated with scenes of hunting among animals of which no trace is preserved. Abbate (ADS 438,  see Disegnatori, p. 419, fig. 246) which also documents a third row. Above it is the complex scenography with two-storey architectures animated by figures of gods and heroes made of polychrome stucco of which in some cases only the imprint remains, which nevertheless allows the scene represented to be perfectly recognized.

Gymnasium (C): detail of the S section of the W wall with the mondòpteros in the center under which Heracles, drunk, with club and lion advances with an uncertain step on a ladder, while a young Satyr climbs the last steps to reach him and extends his hand to collect the contents of the cup (or a rhytòn according to the tempera of Abbate v. Disegnatori,  p. 419, fig. 246) that the hero holds in his right hand. The columns are replaced by palm trees and two swans on the volutes of the pediment of the door, covering the architrave. On the roof there is a female figure in the pose of the pòtnia theron, probably Diana flanked by two fawns. The figures of Satyrs coming out of the doors of the side aedicules and those of the horses represented in the small paintings with doors supported by Victories, which were located above the partitions on the sides of the monòpteros, and the dolphins, the /yrae, the birds, the craters, the racemes present in the plinth of the scenography, were still executed in stucco.  as well as the quarters placed as partitions of the side views, the one on the left with Hylas and the nymphs and the one on the right with Perseus and Andromeda seated on the edge of a cave below which the sea monster can be seen, while a personification of the place sits on the far left. This depiction has also been interpreted as Satyr and Maenad, Triton and Nereid or Nymphs seated on a cave. The first interpretation is preferable as that subject, together with that of the other partition, is connected to Heracles, of whom Perseus is an ancestor and Hylas a close friend, in the complete composition of theatrical scenography. At the bottom of the wings closed by these partitions were painted views of the landscape that have now completely vanished, as well as the flying figures of the upper part.

The young man, with two skewers in his left hand, an oînochoòe in his right and his cloak fluttering behind his shoulders, flees from a kneeling Nymph holding an urn on her legs; on the left another Nymph turns backwards leaning on a small pillar on which is the urn from which abundant water falls and a third seated on the rocks closes the composition.

38. Gymnasium (C), S-section of the gate of (F). Detail of the scenography in polychrome stucco with a Doric door open on a staircase at the top of which is a Satyr advancing to the left, with a tympanon in the lowered right; according to the documentation left to us by G. Abbate (see Disegnatori, p. 419, fig. 246), a four-sided portico-seen in perspective and interrupted on the front side crowned by volutes, is surmounted on the back side by a candelabrum; in the large window on the right, closed at the bottom by a gate, there are figures of a Silenus and a young Satyr seated on it, intent on drinking.

39. Gymnasium (C), S-section of the gate of (F). Detail of the area above that of the previous photo, with architecture articulated in pergolas, windows and loggias within which you can see the remains of figures in motion. Still recognizable is the naked female figure who advances with a dancing step inside the large window in opus quadrata; no longer visible is the reclining figure, in the act of drinking from a rhyton, which Abbate has represented (see Disegnatori, p. 419, fig. 246) on the architrave below the left curtain. Gymnasium (C): the pillar between the nymphaeum (G) and the corridor (H) has a stucco panel on the face towards the gymnasium, still preserved in the condition in which it was found, with Daedalus and Icarus. The scene is that of the manufacture of the wings that the ingenious craftsman is completing; one has already been applied to the back of the young man who, standing, looks towards his father and the latter, sitting at the workbench, is arranging the support corrections to the other. 45. Nymphaeum (F). Currently, the decoration of wall O (see fig. 40), which is best documented by this shot, can hardly be distinguished. On the sides of the niche from which the water necessary for the foot bath flowed, the function for which this room was used, were painted statues of Nymphs-Fountain holding shells from which water falls and are flanked by garden views. On the right you can see a large bird, perched on the balustrade, "the large green bird, which looks like a peacock" mentioned by Minervini (BAN 1855, p. 134). On each wall, on the sides of the doors and in the corners, among the plants of the gardens there were also statues of crouching androsphinxes which, with their Egyptian characterization, constituted a link with the Nilotic scenes populated by pygmies and crocodiles present on panels placed as a plinth and alternating with other panels with a yellow background with sea monsters in brown chiaroscuro. On the left wall, among the trees and bushes, was the statue of a Satyr with nebride pedums in a dancing attitude, with his right hand raised to hold a tankard.

Nymphaeum (F): the ceiling of the niche on the W wall was decorated with glass mosaic, while the walls had a limestone cladding to obtain the effect of a cave with stalactites and the corners were marked by rows of cardium edule shells. 47. Nymphaeum (G), W wall. The Nilotic subject of ducks in a swamp with marsh plants returned in the mosaic panel with glass tiles that completed the ceiling of the niche on this wall.

49. Corridor (H) led to the secondary entrance on Vicolo del Lupanare, recovering with its slope a difference in height of about 1 m from E to W. The walls, originally in opus incerta, underwent reconstructions in brick work and in opus vittata in correspondence with the windows of (S) and (T); At a height of 5 m there are holes for the floor beams. The plaster imitated bardiglio slabs with veins arranged in a herringbone pattern in the plinth, while the middle area was simply white.

50. The corridor (]), also open onto Vicolo del Lupanare, retains the vaulted roof in which six skylights open. On the N side are the four small single bathrooms (N1-N4) that are part, with a fifth (N5) later transformed into the antechamber of the latrine (O), of the oldest nucleus of the baths. The cladding consists only of rough plaster.

51. corridor (K) which ends on the outside with the beautiful tuff portal of number 48 was already in use in the first phase of construction of the complex when it allowed access to rooms (II)-(III) later transformed into (O)-(O"), (11) and (10), and the remains of the decoration of the first style recognizable in the protruding frame that runs along the walls belong to this period (second half of the second century BC). The floor in rhomboidal terracotta tiles with a border of white tiles is contemporary with that of the apoditerium

52. Latrine (O): this important room was placed in part of room (I) (cf. Eschebach ST, tav. 36) next to which was the well (M), one of the oldest in Pompeii, whose water was brought to the surface through a water wheel operated by hand by slaves condemned in antliam, and collected in a cistern placed above the latrine. It was accessed from the S when one of the small rooms for the single bathroom was abolished. Along the walls there are the balconies, in limestone and brick blocks, for the wooden planks of the seats and in the floor runs a channel covered with cocciopesto through which the room was cleaned, supplied with clean water from inlet pipes present in the N-W and SE corners.

The two-storey architectural foreshortening had a cinnabar red background that faded into black despite the fact that the penetration of the sun's rays into the environment was reduced to a minimum.

Antechamber (1): the lunette on the W wall shows in the centre, under an aedicule with doors on which small pictures with doors rest, and semicircular wings with lacunar ceilings, a Nereid on a sea monster and on the sides two cupids holding garlands hanging from the architectural structure; from the ends of this hang two festoons wrapped in bandages that connect with the wide turned ribbon that is suspended in several points of the frame interrupted by squares and medallions.

61. Antechamber (1): the decoration of the vault in polychrome stucco does not have a centripetal motif but unfolds in a network of medallions with a blue background with tabbed frames and red garlands, containing cupids and animals connected by ribbons that determine octagonal fields with concave sides. In eight of them with a blue background there is no internal frame so that the resulting space is greater and they had painted or relief figures. Of the painted figures, the one of a young man with a cloak on his shoulders is recognizable in the S section, traces of a similar figure can be recognized in the N, while in the O a figure of Eros can be sensed, and in the fourth field no trace of color remains; the relief figures were those of the Seasons; in the framed octagons there are sea monsters and swans. Gigante (Eschebach ST, fig. 40 b; see Disegnatori, p. 996, fig. 17), retained no trace of any window. The floor, like that of the antechamber, is made of marble slabs.

75. Male apoditerium (2): the same room after the reconstruction of the vault that most emphasized the asymmetrical structure of the archivolts, in ancient times less visible due to the rich stucco decoration that covered them entirely together with the vaults.

76. Male apoditerium (2): in the lunette E the lower part and about a quarter of the S part are preserved. At the center of an architectural structure articulated on two floors there is a large Delphic tripod on which rests an archaistic Apollo behind which the remains of the serpent's coils can be glimpsed. Under the side aedicules, decorated with garlands and clypei are cupids on dolphins and statues of Hermaphrodite. Of the figures in the upper part, only part of a figure on the throne remains. A frame with ovals and leaves emphasizes the connection between the lunette and the vault.

77. Male apoditerium (2), lunette E: detail of the cupid on a dolphin of the S section. The imagines clipeatae are characterized as barbarians with rough features, beards and thick hair. The frame with circumscribed palmettes and lotus buds that emphasizes the bowstring is executed with particular care and the imprint of the matrix in the center of the lotuses is visible.
